newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST -Spanish bill yields to pick up at auction.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Spanish bill yields to pick up at auction.

text.p: Recent jitters over the future of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) are seen pushing yields higher at Wednesday's Spanish Treasury auction of one-year and 18-month bills, dealers said on Tuesday.

According to grey-market prices, one-year bill yields should emerge at around 5.02/5.06 percent, while 18-month bills should be at 5.05/5.10 percent. At the previous auction two weeks ago, they were respectively 4.975 percent and 5.005 percent.
"European tensions pushed money market rates higher, and that had an effect on bill yields (on the secondary market) as well," a dealer said.
Despite market expectations for benign May inflation data, to be released on Friday, dealers said the Bank of Spain was unlikely to use the scope it has to cut its key rate as soon as next week.
They added it was more likely the central bank would wait for more stable markets and a clearer EMU outlook.
"Now the market is not discounting an immediate fall in interest rates and it seems it is not pricing in expectations for positive CPI data," a dealer said.
"The Bank of Spain has already said that market stability is a decisive factor in its decisions on rates and this moment does not seem quite right," he added.
One dealer said that investment trusts were pushing rates higher.
On Friday, 492.8 billion pesetas worth of one-year bills will mature.
